item.title: ABOUT
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
INTRODUCTION

Building digital products with a focus on human intent and structural clarity.

My Story

I am a product designer currently based in London, where I focus on crafting experiences that balance business objectives with deep user empathy. My journey began in architectural studies, where I learned the importance of foundational systems and spatial logic—principles I now apply to the digital landscape.

Over the past eight years, I have worked with startups and established enterprises to define their visual languages and product strategies. I believe that good design is quiet; it should facilitate a user's goals without demanding unnecessary attention.

How I do it

Structural Integrity

Systems-first approach that ensures scalability and long-term maintenance of digital ecosystems.

Intentional Craft

Every pixel serves a purpose. I avoid decorative clutter in favor of meaningful, high-contrast interactions.

Empathy First

Deep research into human behavior drives every decision, ensuring the product resonates on an emotional level.

INFORMATION

Common inquiries

I work across product design, brand identity, and visual systems — from early-stage startups building their first app to established companies looking to sharpen how they show up in the world. If there's a real problem to solve and intention behind the work, I'm interested.

Every project starts with discovery — understanding your audience, your goals, and the gap between where you are and where you want to be. From there I move through strategy, concept, and execution, but it's never a rigid waterfall. Good design is iterative, and I stay close to the work at every stage.

Both. I've worked with founders on day one and with teams that have been around for decades. The stage matters less than the clarity of intent. If you know what you're trying to build — even roughly — we can work from there.

It depends on scope. A focused brand identity usually runs four to six weeks. A full product design engagement can span several months. I'd rather give you an honest timeline upfront than rush something that needs room to breathe.

Mostly: context, candor, and a willingness to push past the obvious. The best briefs aren't necessarily the most detailed — they're the most honest. Tell me what you're building, who it's for, and what success looks like. We'll figure out the rest together.

item.title: Flow Finance
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
UX/UI DESIGN

Flow Finance

Personal finance apps are notoriously overwhelming, presenting users with walls of charts and daunting terminology. Flow approached me with a different goal: design a money management tool that feels as effortless and intuitive as messaging a friend.

ROLE

Lead Product Designer

TIMELINE

6 Months (Q3 2024)

DELIVERABLES

Web App, Design System

TOOLS

Figma, ProtoPie, Maze

MY APPROACH TO THE

The problem

Young professionals are dealing with unprecedented financial anxiety. They ignore their budgets because the interfaces remind them of tedious accounting software. The challenge was to translate complex financial data into a calm, rewarding user experience that encourages daily check-ins rather than avoiding the app altogether.

item.title: Kora Roasters
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
BRAND IDENTITY

Kora Roasters

Specialty coffee is often perceived as an exclusive club — full of complex terminology and a snobbish attitude. Kora came to me with a clear vision: create a visual identity that brings premium coffee to everyday people without losing authenticity.

ROLE

Art Director

TIMELINE

3 Months (Q2 2024)

DELIVERABLES

Logo, Brand Guidelines

TOOLS

Illustrator, InDesign

MY APPROACH TO THE

The problem

Traditional coffee brands rely on dark colors and a minimalist, almost cold aesthetic. The challenge was to disrupt this stereotype with playful typography and bold colors, making the brand feel approachable while retaining credibility among hardcore coffee enthusiasts.

item.title: Rombo Pick
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
PRODUCT DESIGN

Rombo Pick

The guitar pick is one of the most overlooked objects in music — used thousands of times a day, almost never designed with intention. Rombo came to me with a simple challenge: make something a musician would actually want to hold.

ROLE

Lead Product Designer

TIMELINE

4 Months (Q1 2024)

DELIVERABLES

Web App, Design System

TOOLS

Figma, Framer, Notion

MY APPROACH TO THE

The problem

As decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) grew, the friction between speed and governance became a critical failure point. High-velocity teams were losing hours to voting bureaucracy, leading to "governance fatigue" and stalled progress on core product initiatives.
